In the sentence "I'll get you some stamps if I go to town," "if I go to town" is a subordinate/dependent clause (= it is not as important as the main part of the sentence and could not exist as a separate sentence).

definition: a. Capable of being decided; determinable.

examples: It's up to you to decide.

For most customers, price is the deciding factor.

That decided it for me: I wasn't carrying my bike back up those stairs.

He decided (that) it was his business.

The deciding factor in choosing this school was that it was far from home.
